description: Severity distribution for electrical contact and arc flash, unmitigated (no PPE, insulation, or lockout). P(death) scale from AIS mortality data.
assumptions: Direct contact or arc flash within flash boundary
Unmitigated: no insulated gloves, no arc-rated PPE, no LOTO
AC current (50/60 Hz) — DC thresholds are ~3-5x higher
Pathway through trunk assumed for worst-case (hand-to-hand or hand-to-foot)

magnitude_bands.description: Extra-low voltage. Battery systems, control circuits, telecoms. Below IEC 60479 safety threshold.
magnitude_bands.mortality_source: IEC 60479-1: body impedance at 50V insufficient to drive dangerous current through intact dry skin
magnitude_bands.rationale: Below 50V AC, current through intact skin is below perception threshold in most conditions. P90 reflects wet-skin contact producing tingling/minor burn. Not SIF-capable except in exceptional circumstances (immersion, broken skin).

magnitude_bands.description: Low voltage. Domestic/light commercial (120V NA, 230V EU). Above let-go threshold.
magnitude_bands.mortality_source: IEC 60479-1: 50-250V spans let-go current (10mA) through VF zone (30-500mA depending on duration). NFPA 70E incident data.
magnitude_bands.rationale: Most domestic electrical contacts produce burns or muscle contraction without cardiac effects. P90 reflects wet-skin hand-to-hand pathway driving VF current (>30mA AC). Let-go threshold ~10mA means victim may be unable to release. Crosses SIF threshold at P90.

magnitude_bands.description: Medium voltage. Industrial 3-phase (380-600V). Arc flash becomes significant.
magnitude_bands.mortality_source: NFPA 70E arc flash boundary calculations; IEEE 1584 incident energy models; OSHA electrical fatality data
magnitude_bands.rationale: At 480V+ the current through body impedance (~1kΩ wet) reaches 0.5A — 10x the VF threshold. Arc flash at these voltages produces 2nd/3rd degree burns. Median outcome is serious injury. P90 fatality from sustained contact or arc blast.

magnitude_bands.description: High voltage. Distribution systems, substations, industrial HV. Arc blast zone extends metres.
magnitude_bands.mortality_source: IEEE 1584: incident energy at HV produces severe burns at distance. Utility worker fatality studies.
magnitude_bands.rationale: Arc flash energy at HV causes severe burns at several metres distance. Direct contact is almost always fatal. P10=0.01 reflects momentary arc exposure at flash boundary edge. P50=0.50 reflects ~40% mortality. Unambiguously SIF.

magnitude_bands.description: Very high voltage. Transmission lines (33kV-400kV+), major substations. Arc flash at distance.
magnitude_bands.mortality_source: Utility sector fatality data; transmission line contact is near-uniformly fatal
magnitude_bands.rationale: At transmission voltages, arc flash produces plasma temperatures >20,000°C and blast pressures sufficient to cause fatal burns and blunt trauma at distance. Direct contact is unsurvivable. P10 reflects arc exposure at extreme edge of flash boundary. P50=0.90 reflects that ~70% of contacts are fatal.

skin_condition.description: Multiplier on effective current (reduces body impedance). IEC 60479-1 shows wet skin impedance ~1/4 of dry. This dramatically changes the risk at low voltages.

pathway.description: Heart current factor from IEC 60479-1. Pathways through the chest have highest cardiac risk.

duration.description: Multiplier on severity. VF risk is duration-dependent (IEC 60479-1 time-current zones). Above let-go threshold, duration is determined by circuit protection (breaker trip time).

current_type.description: Multiplier on P(death) by band. DC is less dangerous than AC at low/medium voltages: VF threshold ~150mA DC vs ~30mA AC (5x), and DC causes throw-off rather than tetanic grip (shorter contact duration). At high voltages the current exceeds all thresholds regardless, so AC/DC converges. IEC 60479-1 Parts 1 (AC) and 4 (DC). Note: DC arc flash (solar, batteries, EV) behaves differently — DC arcs are sustained (no zero crossing to self-extinguish), partially offsetting the lower cardiac risk.

sources.author: IEC 60479-1
sources.relevance: Effects of current on human beings — body impedance, perception/reaction/let-go/VF thresholds, time-current zones

sources.author: NFPA 70E
sources.relevance: Standard for Electrical Safety in the Workplace — arc flash boundary, PPE categories, incident energy calculations

sources.author: IEEE 1584
sources.relevance: Guide for Performing Arc-Flash Hazard Calculations — incident energy vs distance, arc duration, equipment type

sources.author: OSHA
sources.relevance: Electrical fatalities: ~5% of all workplace fatalities. Low-voltage (120-240V) accounts for majority of electrical deaths.

sources.author: Baker et al.
sources.relevance: AIS mortality rates — foundation for P(death) scale mapping

validation_notes: STKY check: 480V unmitigated contact should give P(SIF) > 0.50 — medium band P50=0.10, P(SIF)=0.50 ✓
STKY check: 11kV contact should give P(SIF) near 1.0 — high band, most outcomes serious+ ✓
Cross-check: domestic 120V is ELEVATED not SIF — matches industry practice of requiring GFCI but not full arc flash PPE
Key insight: most electrical workplace deaths are from LOW voltage (120-240V) because exposure frequency is high, not because per-contact severity is highest
